historical_references.reference: The early Christian martyr Clemency, who was reportedly a slave girl, was venerated in Roman North Africa in the 4th century. She was martyred under the Roman Emperor Diocletian for refusing to sacrifice to Roman gods.

Clemency of Richelieu (1585-1642), also known as Armand Jean du Plessis, was a French statesman and cardinal during the reigns of Louis XIII and Louis XIV. He was a major figure in the politics of the time and is remembered for his efforts to bring peace and stability to France, earning the title 'Cardinal of Charity'.
